subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: HTTP Methods Explained
description: A micro-lesson that makes HTTP Methods Explained usable.

hook.text: A developer uses GET to delete a user. It works, but it breaks every caching layer and proxy in between.

buildup.text: HTTP methods define intent: GET reads, POST creates, PUT replaces, PATCH updates, DELETE removes.

discovery.text: Using the correct method ensures caches, proxies, and clients all behave as the protocol expects.

twist.text: Testing verifies that each endpoint uses the correct method and rejects wrong ones with proper errors.

climax.text: A test confirms that DELETE on a read-only resource returns 405 Method Not Allowed. Correct behavior.

punchline.text: GET reads. POST creates. DELETE removes. Test that each does only its job.

quiz.question: What should happen when using the wrong HTTP method on an endpoint?
options: The server should return 405 Method Not Allowed
